about: Starter rule pack. It explains the Papyrus engine's common runtime errors in plain words. Its rules are explain rules, so a match shows as FOUND and never fails a run. Most of these messages come from the base game and other mods too, so look at the script named under each line ('at ...') to see whose error it is.
source: The wording follows the Creation Kit wiki page 'Papyrus Runtime Errors' and the lines Starfield writes to Papyrus.0.log.

explain.re: Cannot call \w+\(\) on a None object
explain.means: A script called a function on a variable or property that was empty (None). The usual cause is a property that was never filled in the Creation Kit, or an object that was deleted or not loaded yet. The script skipped that call and went on.

explain.re: Unable to call \w+ - no native object bound to the script object
explain.means: A script called a built-in function on an object that no longer exists in the game. This happens most often in magic effect scripts after the effect has ended, and with objects inside containers.

explain.re: Cannot add a None reference to the alias
explain.means: A script tried to put an empty reference into a quest alias. The reference it wanted was not found.

explain.re: Cannot access an element of a None array
explain.means: A script read from an array that was never created. The script should check the array before it uses it.

explain.re: Array index -?\d+ is out of range
explain.means: A script asked for an array element that doesn't exist, such as element 5 of a 3-element array.
A script divided by zero. The result is thrown away.

explain.re: Assigning None to a non-object variable named
explain.means: A script stored None in a number, text or true/false variable. This usually follows a failed call: read the error just before this line, which is the real cause.

explain.re: Cannot set the value of a constant GlobalVariable
explain.means: A script tried to change a global variable that is marked Constant in its plugin. The value stays as it was.

explain.re: does not have 3d and cannot have an effect shader played on it
explain.means: A script tried to play a visual effect on an object that isn't drawn at the moment (it is far away, disabled or not loaded yet). This is usually harmless.
A function kept calling itself, or a chain of functions went too deep, and the engine stopped it. Look for a function that calls itself without a way to stop.
